analysis.headline: USD/KRW eases to 1,335.7 in Seoul as exporter selling counters stock rout
analysis.summary: USD/KRW eased 1.0 KRW to close at 1,335.7 KRW in Seoul daytime trading (ECB ref 1,334.87). Despite foreign equity selling on KOSPI tech routs and hawkish Fed rate expectations, aggressive dollar-selling (nego) flows from semiconductor and shipbuilder exporters capped upside at 1,338.6 KRW and held trading in a 1,332.9–1,338.6 KRW band.

analysis.headline: EUR/KRW drops to 1,470.2 KRW as EUR/USD slides toward 1.101 on growth doubts
analysis.summary: EUR/KRW retreated to around 1,470.2 (ECB ref 1,470.23), declining to the lower 1,470 KRW handle. Persistent dollar resilience and weak Eurozone sentiment pushed EUR/USD down toward 1.1011–1.1014. With USD/KRW softening in Seoul, the pronounced weakness in the single currency kept the cross pressured in a 1,466–1,475 KRW range.

analysis.headline: JPY/KRW rebounds to 836.4 per 100 JPY on tech risk-off and BOJ rate hints
analysis.summary: JPY/KRW rebounded to around 8.36 KRW per JPY (~836.4 KRW per 100 JPY, ECB ref 8.364). Global tech equity declines stimulated safe-haven yen demand, while BOJ board member Takata hinted at moving closer to a neutral policy rate. USD/JPY slipped to 159.4, lifting the cross from recent lows within an 832–840 KRW band.

analysis.headline: GBP/KRW softens to 1,761.8 KRW as cable slips below 1.32 against strong dollar
analysis.summary: GBP/KRW eased to around 1,761.8 (ECB ref 1,761.81) within a 1,757–1,768 KRW range. Although the Bank of England’s 4.0% policy rate and stubborn service-sector inflation provided support, broad dollar strength pressed GBP/USD toward 1.3196. Paired with a modest decline in USD/KRW, the cross drifted mildly lower.

analysis.headline: CNY/KRW defends 200.2 mark supported by PBOC fixing and steady Seoul dollar
analysis.summary: CNY/KRW closed steady at around 200.2 (ECB ref 200.24) within a 199.7–200.7 KRW range, maintaining the key 200.0 KRW psychological floor. The PBOC continued its supportive daily fixing strategy and liquidity provisions against broad dollar gains, while stable USD/KRW trading around 1,335 KRW anchored the cross.

AUD.headline: AUD eases to 901.9 KRW on tech-led risk aversion and commodity softness
AUD.brief: The Australian dollar slipped to 901.9 KRW as global tech equity declines and softer commodity prices weighed on risk assets despite the RBA’s hawkish stance.

CAD.headline: CAD dips to 934.4 KRW amid rangebound crude and BoC easing stance
CAD.brief: The Canadian dollar eased to 934.4 KRW, pressured by flat crude oil prices and ongoing BoC-Fed monetary policy divergence alongside a softer USD/KRW in Seoul.

CHF.headline: CHF stays weak at 1,590.5 KRW as elevated US yields curb low-rate havens
CHF.brief: The Swiss franc lingered below 1,600 at 1,590.5 KRW, as persistent high U.S. yields drove outflows from low-yielding havens despite equity market volatility.

CNY.headline: CNY holds 200.2 KRW underpinned by firm PBOC fixing and liquidity aid
CNY.brief: The Chinese yuan held steady at 200.2 KRW; proactive PBOC fixing defenses and liquidity injections cushioned dollar gains while preserving the 200 KRW floor.

EUR.headline: EUR slides to 1,470.2 KRW as EUR/USD retreats toward 1.101 on soft growth
EUR.brief: The euro weakened to 1,470.2 KRW as post-inflation dollar resilience and sluggish Eurozone economic prospects pushed EUR/USD down toward 1.1011.

GBP.headline: GBP eases to 1,761.8 KRW as cable drops below 1.32 despite BoE 4.0% rate
GBP.brief: The British pound drifted to 1,761.8 KRW; steady BoE 4.0% interest rate support was outweighed by dollar gains that pushed cable under 1.32.

HKD.headline: HKD eases to 170.1 KRW reflecting modest USD/KRW pullback in Seoul
HKD.brief: The Hong Kong dollar eased to 170.1 KRW within its peg band, mirroring the small dip in USD/KRW driven by Korean exporter dollar selling.

JPY.headline: JPY firms to 836.4 per 100 JPY on safe-haven flows and BOJ rate comments
JPY.brief: The Japanese yen rebounded to 836.4 KRW per 100 JPY as global tech losses stoked haven bids and BOJ board member Takata voiced openness to further rate hikes.

KRW.headline: KRW firms to 1,335.7 as exporter dollar sales overcome stock sell-off
KRW.brief: The Korean won gained slightly to 1,335.7 per USD, as massive exporter dollar-selling flows absorbed heavy foreign stock divestment and KOSPI weakness.

USD.headline: USD dips to 1,335.7 KRW in Seoul as exporter dollar offers cap gains
USD.brief: The U.S. dollar eased to 1,335.7 KRW (ECB ref 1,334.9) in Seoul trading as abundant exporter dollar supply counterbalanced hawkish Fed rate expectations.
